claims.claim: The studied Pre-Norm models have higher visual-token norms than text-token norms.
claims.evidence: high-norm visual tokens and the low-norm text tokens

claims.claim: The analysis predicts slower semantic changes in high-norm visual tokens.
claims.evidence: transform semantically much slower than their textual counterparts

claims.claim: The proposed norm alignment adds one LayerNorm after the visual projector.
claims.evidence: inserting a single, carefully initialized LayerNorm layer after the visual projector

claims.claim: On LLaVA-1.5, the intervention improved text-only evaluation performance including MMLU.
claims.evidence: on text-only evaluations such as MMLU

claims.claim: HSA allocates sliding-window attention at the level of individual KV heads.
claims.evidence: applies sparsity at the KV-head level

claims.claim: Each HSA layer retains a global attention head.
claims.evidence: at least one full-attention KV head

claims.claim: A post-training discrepancy measure selects heads to retain for global attention.
claims.evidence: discrepancy-based post-training selection strategy

claims.claim: The authors report the clearest advantages over layer-wise sparsity in long contexts.
claims.evidence: advantages being especially significant in long-context scenarios

claims.claim: CoCoMix learns to predict continuous concepts provided by a pretrained sparse autoencoder.
claims.evidence: learned from a pretrained sparse autoencoder

claims.claim: The model interleaves concepts with token representations in its hidden state.
claims.evidence: interleaving with token hidden representations

claims.claim: The authors report better sample efficiency than standard next-token prediction and distillation on the benchmarks studied.
claims.evidence: more sample efficient and consistently outperforms standard next token prediction and knowledge distillation

claims.claim: The predicted concept can be edited to steer the model.
claims.evidence: direct inspection and modification of the predicted concept

claims.claim: The team introduces a five-dimensional assessment for selecting medical multimodal data.
claims.evidence: five-dimensional quality assessment framework

claims.claim: Training uses multimodal sequence packing for efficiency.
claims.evidence: multimodal sequence packing to enhance training efficiency

claims.claim: The medical models undergo three stages of supervised fine-tuning.
claims.evidence: three-stage supervised fine-tuning process

claims.claim: In the reported MedEvalKit evaluation, InfiMed-Foundation-1.7B outperformed Qwen2.5VL-3B.
claims.evidence: InfiMed-Foundation-1.7B outperforms Qwen2.5VL-3B

claims.claim: DuoLLM uses separate streams for semantic and spatial processing.
claims.evidence: decouples semantic and spatial processing

claims.claim: Depth estimation introduces 2.5D geometric information into its spatial stream.
claims.evidence: depth estimation module that introduces 2.5D geometric priors

claims.claim: The relational attention mechanism models spatial relations between objects.
claims.evidence: relational attention mechanism that captures object-to-object spatial dependencies

claims.claim: Asymmetric cross-attention fuses the spatial and semantic features.
claims.evidence: asymmetric cross-attention module that fuses semantic and spatial features

claims.claim: The authors report gains over the evaluated open-source LVLMs on SpatialScore-Hard.
claims.evidence: On the challenging SpatialScore-Hard benchmark, DuoLLM delivers substantial improvements over widely used open-source LVLMs
